name: Kenyon cells (all compartments)
function: Sparse coders of the mushroom body (~2,500 per hemisphere; v783 lists 5,177 total); receive converging sensory-projection input in the calyx; sites of dopaminergic plasticity onto MBONs.
references: Aso et al. 2014 (eLife); Li et al. 2020 (eLife hemibrain MB map)

name: Mushroom-body output neurons (MBON01-35)
region: Mushroom body lobes -> LH, SIP, SMP, crepine
function: Convergent readout of KC activity; compartment-organised; activation of single MBON types is sufficient to drive approach or avoidance behaviour (valence-carrying output).

name: PAM-cluster dopaminergic neurons (PAM01-15)
function: Reward/appetitive reinforcement: PAM neurons convey sugar and water reward to MB compartments; reward-memory formation requires PAM activity.
references: Liu et al. 2012; Aso et al. 2012; Huetteroth et al. 2015; Yamagata et al. 2016; McCurdy et al. 2021
proposed_mapping: REWARD events (game gains: EXP, level-up, item, quest)

name: PPL1-cluster dopaminergic neurons (PPL1-01..08)
function: Punishment/aversive reinforcement: PPL1 neurons convey electric shock and bitter punishment; induce aversive memory; some types signal absolute vs relative punishment.
references: Aso et al. 2010; Aso et al. 2012; McCloy et al. 2022 (biorxiv)

name: PPL2-cluster dopaminergic neurons (PPL2-01..04)
function: Dopaminergic cluster with less completely characterised behavioural roles; registered, not used initially.
references: FlyWire v783 annotations; Kong et al. 2017

name: Anterior paired lateral (APL) neuron
function: Giant GABAergic feedback neuron providing normalisation / gain control and negativ feedback onto KCs; anti-Hebbian opponent in some plasticity models.
references: Inada et al. 2017; Papadopoulou et al. 2013; Masquez et al. 2018

name: Dorsal paired medial (DPM) neuron
function: Neuromodulatory feedback neuron required for memory consolidation; releases 5-HT and peptides across MB lobes.
references: Yu et al. 2005; Yu et al. 2015; Scheffer et al. 2020

name: Dopaminergic DESCENDING neurons (DopaMeander candidates)
function: Dopaminergic modulatory descending neurons; Liessem et al. (2026) show the DopaMeander DAN-DNs drive forward walking with increased ipsiversive turning. v783 contains 7 dopaminergic DNs; the exact DopaMeander correspondence is not yet published in ID-resolved form.
